blocks.text: The hidden cost of manual gallery delivery

Every minute you spend manually uploading files to a gallery platform is a minute you are not shooting or editing. This administrative burden adds up quickly. If you handle ten shoots a month, you might spend hundreds of hours per year on tasks that do not require your creative input. This is not just lost time. It is lost revenue and increased mental fatigue. When you are tired from repetitive clicks, your creative work suffers. You might miss small details in your edits or delay communication with your next client. This creates a cycle where you feel behind even when you are working hard.
Why your current workflow causes burnout

The main cause of this problem is context switching. You move from editing in Lightroom to emailing a link in Gmail, then to your accounting software to check for a payment. Each shift requires you to hold new information in your head. This fragmentation is the primary driver of professional burnout. It makes you feel like you are always working but never finished. Because your systems are often disconnected, you end up doing the same work twice. You might rename a file in Finder, then realize you need to rename it again within your gallery software. These small, redundant tasks are the silent killers of your business efficiency.
Fixing your workflow without spending money

items: Consolidate your folders. Use a consistent naming convention in Finder immediately upon import.
Use templates. Save your email responses for delivery in Gmail as canned responses.
Batch your tasks. Do not upload galleries one by one. Set aside one afternoon for all deliveries.
Clear your desktop. Use a dedicated folder for all client assets to avoid searching through random files.
Use macOS Shortcuts. Create a simple shortcut to move files from your camera card to your project folder.
